title: “Walk me through” scenarios
objectives: Answer out loud: Buy $100 of PP&E.
Answer out loud: All in under 45 seconds each.

blocks.body: Use the same method every time: **IS → CFS → BS, then check that it balances.** Assume a 40% tax rate unless told otherwise.

blocks.template: Buy $100 of PP&E with cash → net income {{1}}, cash {{2}}
Repay $50 of debt principal → income statement impact: {{1}}
Stock-based comp of $10 → net income {{1}}, cash {{2}}, equity {{3}}

blocks.title: Depreciation goes up by $10 — walk me through it.
blocks.body: **Interview answer:** "Operating income falls by $10, so at a 40% tax rate net income falls by $6. On the cash flow statement, net income is down $6 but we add back the $10 of depreciation since it's non-cash, so cash is up $4. On the balance sheet, cash is up $4, PP&E is down $10, so assets are down $6. Retained earnings is down $6, so both sides are down $6 and it balances."

blocks.title: Why does depreciation *increase* cash?
blocks.body:
Depreciation is tax-deductible but non-cash. It lowers taxable income, so the company pays less tax. The cash increase is the tax shield: $10 × 40% = $4.

**Interview answer:** "It reduces taxes without using cash, so cash goes up by depreciation times the tax rate."

blocks.prompt: Depreciation increases by $10 with a 40% tax rate. What happens to cash?
blocks.explanation: Net income falls $6, but the $10 non-cash charge is added back, so cash rises by the $4 tax shield ($10 × 40%).

blocks.title: Inventory written down by $10.
blocks.teaser: Same mechanics as depreciation: non-cash expense.
blocks.body: Same mechanics as depreciation: non-cash expense. Net income −$6, add back $10 → cash +$4. BS: cash +$4, inventory −$10 → assets −$6; equity −$6. (Assumes the write-down is tax-deductible, the standard interview simplification.)

blocks.title: Raise $100 of debt, then pay $10 of interest.
blocks.teaser: Raising debt: no IS impact; CFF +$100; cash and debt both +$100.
blocks.body: Raising debt: no IS impact; CFF +$100; cash and debt both +$100. Paying interest: net income −$6; cash −$6; equity −$6. Interest is tax-deductible, so the after-tax cost is only $6.

blocks.title: Repay $50 of debt principal.
blocks.teaser: No IS impact — principal isn't an expense.
blocks.body:
No IS impact — principal isn't an expense. CFF −$50. Cash −$50, debt −$50.

**Interview answer:** "Principal repayment never hits the income statement. Cash and debt both fall by $50."

blocks.title: Stock-based compensation of $10.
blocks.body:
IS: −$10 expense → net income −$6. CFS: add back $10 (non-cash) → cash +$4. BS: cash +$4; equity: retained earnings −$6 but common stock/APIC +$10 → equity +$4. Balanced.

**Interview answer:** "Net income falls $6, we add back the $10 since it's non-cash, cash is up $4. Equity is up $4 because the new stock issued adds $10 while retained earnings falls $6."

blocks.title: AR increases by $10 (sale made on credit).
blocks.body: Revenue +$10 → net income +$6. CFS: net income +$6, subtract $10 increase in AR → cash −$4 (you paid tax on revenue you haven't collected). BS: cash −$4, AR +$10 → assets +$6; equity +$6.

blocks.title: A customer prepays $10 (deferred revenue).
blocks.teaser: No revenue yet → no IS impact.
blocks.body: No revenue yet → no IS impact. CFS: deferred revenue up $10 → cash +$10. BS: cash +$10, deferred revenue (liability) +$10. In reality the cash may be taxed when received; the interview version ignores that.

blocks.title: $10 bonus expensed but not yet paid (accrued expense).
blocks.body: Net income −$6. CFS: add back $10 increase in accrued expenses → cash +$4. BS: cash +$4; liabilities +$10; equity −$6.

blocks.title: Pay a $10 dividend.
blocks.body: No IS impact. CFF −$10. Cash −$10, retained earnings −$10.

blocks.title: Buy $10 of inventory with cash, then sell it for $15.
blocks.teaser: Buying: no IS impact; CFO −$10 (inventory up); cash −$10, inventory +$10.
blocks.body: Buying: no IS impact; CFO −$10 (inventory up); cash −$10, inventory +$10. Selling: revenue $15, COGS $10 → pre-tax $5 → net income +$3. CFS: net income +$3, inventory decrease +$10 → +$13. Combined across both steps, cash +$3, which matches net income.
